title: Because metas owns metasfresh, an append-only record of document completion is a feature it can sell
content:
metasfresh is metas's own ERP product, not a third-party system the firm implements for others. That changes what the fit is. An append-only record of document completion, independent of the ERP's mutable tables, becomes a feature metas can add to something it already sells rather than a service delivered once at one client.

The technical gap is the familiar ERP one. Documents move through states and the tables hold the latest state, so completion — this document is final — is a business event read back out of a mutable row. Anyone relying on it has to trust the row's current contents and the discipline of everything that can write to it.

Ownership is what makes this commercially different from the same gap at an implementation partner. The counterpart controls the roadmap, so the record layer can ship as part of the product and reach every installation, and the conversation is about product differentiation rather than about one customer's audit requirement.
